lesson.title: Provider and deployer tests for the new prohibitions
lesson.summary: Apply the distinct supply and use qualifications for the new synthetic-media prohibitions.

prerequisites.reason: Misuse is defined by departure from the system's intended purpose.
The use test depends on the purpose of the deployer.
The learner must apply the separate start date of the new prohibitions.
The market/service test differs from the prohibition on a deployer's use.
The market/service test needs the intimate-media scope and its manipulation boundary.
The market/service test also applies to the incorporated child-abuse material/performance scope.

blocks: For new points (ba)/(bb), paragraph 1a qualifies the supply side. Placement or service is prohibited where generating/manipulating the specified material is the system's intended purpose, or under the alternative foreseeable/reproducible-outcome test.
An imagined theoretical possibility alone is not the same as that second branch. Keep the material category, actor and regulated action in the record.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1a)(a), 5(1a)(b), 5(1b); Article 3(13); Article 113(a)

blocks: The alternative supply branch examines design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing features: the generation must be reasonably foreseeable and reproducible without significant technical modification, and reasonable/adequate safeguards to reliably prevent and correct observed/reported misuse must be absent.
The **supplier-safeguards test** is substantive. A policy statement alone does not establish technical protection; equally, do not assume any conceivable misuse proves the entire branch.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1a)(a), 5(1a)(b), 5(1b); Article 3(13); Article 113(a)

blocks: On the use side, paragraph 1a(b) prohibits the specified generation/manipulation only where the **deployer uses the system for that purpose**. The supply and use tests are different.

Fictional Northbridge case: a general tool's supplier has adequate safeguards, but a deployer intentionally uses it for the specified prohibited material. A favourable supply-side finding cannot automatically cure the separate use-side purpose.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1a)(a), 5(1a)(b), 5(1b); Article 3(13); Article 113(a)

blocks: Record intended purpose; foreseeable, reproducible output; technical modification needed; safeguard adequacy; and deployer purpose separately. Keep point (ba)'s manipulation boundary and the 2 December 2026 date in the full test.
These statutory qualifications concern the new points, not a universal rewriting of every Article 5 prohibition. The case uses non-graphic descriptions and does not demonstrate harmful generation.
